title: 2026-11-17_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_67d
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised Linux host that appears to be infected with the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activity, then contain and remediate the threat.
outcomes: Identify suspicious services and their behavior

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised Linux host that appears to be infected with the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activity, then contain and remediate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (192.168.50.5) using SSH with the provided credentials.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (192.168.50.5) using SSH with the provided credentials.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using SSH with the provided credentials.
2. List all services, including inactive ones, to identify suspicious components:
   ```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
   ```
3. Look for services with unusual names or descriptions. Pay attention to services that might be related to network communication.
4. Identify the suspicious service named "systemkernelservicedefender".

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content:
Use this command to list all services, including inactive ones:
```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions that might indicate malicious activity.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Pay attention to services that might be related to network communication, as the backdoor is known to establish C2 communication.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Examine the suspicious service identified in Task 1:
   ```
systemctl cat systemkernelservicedefender
   ```
2. Look for the ExecStart parameter in the service definition to identify the port number used for communication.
3. Alternatively, use the following command to list listening ports and associated processes:
   ```
ss -tulnp
   ```
4. Identify the port number 80 as the one associated with the suspicious service.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery for Data Collection Service
levels.content: Investigators suspect that unauthorized activity automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers to identify the component responsible for scheduling the unauthorized activity:
   ```
systemctl list-timers --all
   ```
2. Look for timers associated with the suspicious service identified in Task 1.
3. Identify the timer named "lab-checkin.timer" as the component responsible for scheduling the activity.
4. Examine the timer to understand its schedule and behavior:
   ```
systemctl cat lab-checkin.timer
   ```
